metric_def: Whole extent of a function (ours: symbol table; original: up to the next start). Data words and what follows the last ret are left out. Masked: jump labels, call targets, address constants (#%XXXX >= 0x3000 and displacements >= 0x3000), the two encodings of a frame operand (%0000(r15) and @r15). Compared: the sequence of instructions. Levels: exact (same sequence), order (same instructions in another order), differs (n = instructions not matched in an alignment).

<name of our function>.ours: start and end in our binary (hex)
<name of our function>.pairing_evidence: how it is confirmed (caller, string, body) or why it is only automatic
<name of our function>.level: exact | order | differs (n) | own | not codgen code
<name of our function>.classes: list of D1..D14 that explain the differences, or empty

findings.kind: pairing | source | order | dead | data | D1..D14
findings.where: source file and function, or a line range
findings.detail: what differs, with original address and instruction range
findings.action: the change to make, complete enough to do without new analysis

findings_pending.detail: the original crt0 calls 0x4868, which passes argc and argv to the body at 0x023c; ours calls the body directly
findings_pending.action: add to gen3.c, between mycanon and stoasg, a function main(argc, argv) that returns the body; rename the body in main3.c (not main); crt0 then calls the forwarder. Check the bytes of gen3 after the change (the return value needs no extra code if it is returned directly).
findings_pending.result: 0x4868 is a separate function (after a ret at 0x4866, no jumps into it). Its only reference is the call from the start code at 0x1e. Body: spill argc/argv as one long, load them into r7 and r6, call the body at 0x023c, return. Position: in the original it lies between mycanon (0x4804) and stoasg (0x487e), i.e. at the place of a function of gen3.c; our gen3.c has no function there (mycanon is followed by stoasg). Conclusion: the original gen3.c contains a two-argument function that forwards to the body of main (main3.c, 0x023c), and this forwarder is the linked symbol main (crt0 calls it). The body in main3.c must then have another name (a static or differently named function); the name does not appear in the bytes, the link does.
